title: 1969 AHSME Problem 30
statement: Let \(P\) be a point of hypotenuse \(AB\) (or its extension) of isosceles right triangle \(ABC.\) Let \(s=AP^2+PB^2.\) Then:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: \(s\lt2CP^2\) for a finite number of positions of \(P\)

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: \(s\lt2CP^2\) for an infinite number of positions of \(P\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
\(s=2CP^2\) only if \(P\) is the midpoint of \(AB\) or an
endpoint of \(AB\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: \(s\gt2CP^2\) if \(P\) is a trisection point of \(AB\)

solutions.text:
Take \(A=(-a,0),\) \(B=(a,0),\) \(C=(0,a),\) and \(P=(p,0).\) This describes every point on the hypotenuse line. Then \[ \begin{aligned} s&=(p+a)^2+(p-a)^2\\ &=2p^2+2a^2,\\ 2CP^2&=2(p^2+a^2)\\ &=2p^2+2a^2. \end{aligned} \] Thus \(s=2CP^2\) for every position of \(P.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Put the midpoint of \(AB\) at the origin and \(AB\) on the \(x\)-axis
